attractions.name: Maasai Mara
attractions.desc: Home to the wildebeest migration between July and September, when over a million animals cross crocodile-filled rivers in one of nature's most dramatic annual events. Dense predator populations, including lions, cheetahs, and leopards, make game drives here productive year-round, not just during migration season. Maasai-guided village visits add cultural context alongside the wildlife.

attractions.name: Amboseli National Park
attractions.desc: Famous for large elephant herds photographed against the towering backdrop of Mount Kilimanjaro just across the border in Tanzania. The park's swampy wetlands, fed by underground rivers from the mountain, sustain wildlife even through the driest months. Clear morning light before clouds gather around the peak offers the best photography conditions.

attractions.name: Lake Nakuru
attractions.desc: A soda lake once famous for enormous flocks of flamingos, whose numbers now fluctuate with changing water chemistry, alongside a well-protected rhino sanctuary within the park boundaries. Acacia woodland surrounding the lake supports leopards and a healthy giraffe population. Its relatively compact size makes for efficient game drives compared to larger parks.

attractions.name: Diani Beach
attractions.desc: White sand and a protected coral reef on the Indian Ocean coast, a natural and relaxing add-on after the intensity of a safari itinerary. Kitesurfing conditions here are considered among the best in East Africa. A nearby forest reserve protects rare Angolan colobus monkeys, offering a wildlife encounter distinct from the inland parks.

attractions.name: Hell's Gate National Park
attractions.desc: One of the few Kenyan parks where visitors can walk, cycle, or rock climb among wildlife without a vehicle, its dramatic gorge and towering cliffs partly inspiring scenes in Disney's The Lion King. Geothermal activity, including steam vents and hot springs, adds an unusual volcanic backdrop. It's a favorite for a more active, hands-on safari experience.

attractions.name: Nairobi National Park
attractions.desc: An unusual park sitting directly against the edge of a capital city, its lions and rhinos visible with the Nairobi skyline as an incongruous backdrop. It offers a convenient way to see wildlife on a tight schedule or as an introduction before heading further afield. The adjoining Giraffe Centre and elephant orphanage are popular add-ons.

itinerary.label: Days 1–3
itinerary.title: Maasai Mara
itinerary.desc: Morning and evening game drives, with a full day near the Mara River during migration season.
itinerary.cost: Park entry fees run about $80–100/day for non-residents, often bundled into lodge or camp packages.
itinerary.food: Most camps include full board; a bush breakfast set up mid-game-drive is a common, memorable touch.

itinerary.label: Days 4–5
itinerary.title: Amboseli
itinerary.desc: Transfer south for elephant sightings with Kilimanjaro views.
itinerary.cost: Park entry costs about $60–80/day for non-residents.
itinerary.food: Same as the Mara — meals are typically included with your lodge stay here.

itinerary.label: Day 6
itinerary.title: Lake Nakuru
itinerary.desc: A stop for flamingos and a chance at rhino before heading back north.
itinerary.cost: Park entry costs about $50–60/day for non-residents.
itinerary.food: A packed lunch from your previous lodge is the practical choice, since this is often a transit-day stop.

itinerary.label: Day 7
itinerary.title: Nairobi
itinerary.desc: Visit the Giraffe Centre or Sheldrick elephant orphanage before departure.
itinerary.cost: The Sheldrick Wildlife Trust suggests a small entry donation (~$7); the Giraffe Centre costs about $12.
itinerary.food: Try a Nairobi restaurant specializing in nyama choma for a proper send-off meal before departure.

goodToKnow.tipping: USD 10–20/day for safari guides is standard practice
goodToKnow.safety: Safaris are well organized; use reputable operators and avoid walking alone at night in cities
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Domestic flights link parks quickly; road transfers between parks can take most of a day
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (NBO) is the main gateway for this route, with onward domestic flights or road transfers to each park

food.name: Nyama choma
food.desc: Grilled meat, usually goat or beef, slow-cooked over charcoal and a centerpiece of Kenyan social gatherings.

food.name: Ugali
food.desc: A firm maize-flour porridge served as the starchy base for most Kenyan meals.

food.name: Sukuma wiki
food.desc: Sautéed collard greens, a everyday side dish whose name translates roughly to 'stretch the week'.

food.name: Chai
food.desc: Spiced milk tea, brewed strong and sweet, drunk throughout the day.

faq.q: Do I need a visa for Kenya?
faq.a: Technically an eTA rather than a traditional visa — apply online at least 3 days before travel (about $32.50), valid for a single entry.

faq.q: Which airport should I fly into?
faq.a: Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International (NBO), the main gateway with onward domestic flights or road transfers to each park.

faq.q: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination?
faq.a: Only if arriving from a country where yellow fever is endemic — otherwise not required, but check current guidance based on your specific travel history.

faq.q: How much should I tip safari guides?
faq.a: USD 10–20 per day per guide is standard practice, generally handed directly at the end of your stay.

daysReason: 7 days covers Maasai Mara, Amboseli, and Lake Nakuru at a good safari pace. 4–5 works for just the Mara; 10+ lets you add the Kenyan coast or slow the parks down.
visa: An Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) — not a traditional visa — is required in advance for most nationalities, about $32.50, applied for at least 3 days before travel — always confirm current rules before booking.

attractions.name: Maasai Mara
attractions.desc: Casa da migração dos gnus entre julho e setembro, quando mais de um milhão de animais atravessam rios cheios de crocodilos num dos eventos mais dramáticos da natureza. As densas populações de predadores, incluindo leões, chitas e leopardos, tornam os safaris produtivos durante todo o ano, não só na época da migração. Visitas a aldeias Maasai guiadas acrescentam contexto cultural à vida selvagem.

attractions.name: Amboseli
attractions.desc: Famoso pelas grandes manadas de elefantes fotografadas com o imponente Monte Kilimanjaro ao fundo, do outro lado da fronteira na Tanzânia. As zonas húmidas do parque, alimentadas por rios subterrâneos vindos da montanha, sustentam a vida selvagem mesmo nos meses mais secos. A luz suave da manhã, antes de as nuvens se juntarem à volta do pico, oferece as melhores condições fotográficas.

attractions.name: Lago Nakuru
attractions.desc: Um lago de soda outrora famoso por enormes bandos de flamingos, cujo número agora varia com a química da água, ao lado de um santuário de rinocerontes bem protegido dentro do parque. A floresta de acácias que rodeia o lago sustenta leopardos e uma saudável população de girafas. O tamanho relativamente compacto permite safaris eficientes comparado com parques maiores.

attractions.name: Praia de Diani
attractions.desc: Areia branca e um recife de coral protegido na costa do Índico, um complemento natural e relaxante depois da intensidade de um safari. As condições para kitesurf aqui contam-se entre as melhores da África Oriental. Uma reserva florestal próxima protege colobos-pretos angolanos, um encontro com vida selvagem distinto dos parques do interior.

attractions.name: Parque Nacional de Hell's Gate
attractions.desc: Um dos poucos parques quenianos onde se pode caminhar, pedalar ou fazer escalada entre vida selvagem sem veículo, com o seu desfiladeiro dramático e falésias imponentes a inspirar parcialmente cenas de O Rei Leão da Disney. A atividade geotérmica, incluindo fontes de vapor e termas, acrescenta um pano de fundo vulcânico invulgar. É uma escolha preferida para um safari mais ativo e prático.

attractions.name: Parque Nacional de Nairobi
attractions.desc: Um parque invulgar situado mesmo junto aos limites de uma capital, com leões e rinocerontes visíveis tendo o horizonte de Nairobi como pano de fundo incongruente. Oferece uma forma conveniente de ver vida selvagem com pouco tempo disponível ou como introdução antes de seguir mais para o interior. O Centro das Girafas e o orfanato de elefantes adjacentes são acrescentos populares.

itinerary.label: Dias 1–3
itinerary.title: Maasai Mara
itinerary.desc: Safaris de manhã e à tarde, com um dia inteiro perto do Rio Mara durante a época da migração.
itinerary.logistics: ~1h de voo ou 5-6h de carro desde Nairobi

itinerary.label: Dias 4–5
itinerary.title: Amboseli
itinerary.desc: Transferência para sul para avistamentos de elefantes com vista para o Kilimanjaro.

itinerary.label: Dia 6
itinerary.title: Lago Nakuru
itinerary.desc: Uma paragem para flamingos e uma possível oportunidade de ver rinocerontes antes de seguir para norte.
itinerary.logistics: ~4h de carro desde Amboseli via Nairobi

itinerary.label: Dia 7
itinerary.title: Nairobi
itinerary.desc: Visita ao Centro das Girafas ou ao orfanato de elefantes Sheldrick antes da partida.
itinerary.logistics: ~2h de carro desde o Lago Nakuru

goodToKnow.tipping: 10–20 USD/dia para guias de safari é habitual
goodToKnow.safety: Os safaris são bem organizados; usa operadores de confiança e evita andar sozinho à noite nas cidades
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Voos domésticos ligam rapidamente os parques; as transferências por estrada podem demorar quase um dia inteiro
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (NBO) is the main gateway for this route, with onward domestic flights or road transfers to each park

food.name: Nyama choma
food.desc: Carne grelhada, normalmente cabra ou vaca, cozinhada lentamente sobre carvão — o centro de qualquer convívio queniano.

food.name: Ugali
food.desc: Uma papa firme de farinha de milho, servida como base da maioria das refeições quenianas.

food.name: Sukuma wiki
food.desc: Couve salteada, um acompanhamento diário cujo nome se traduz aproximadamente como 'esticar a semana'.

food.name: Chai
food.desc: Chá de leite especiado, forte e doce, bebido ao longo do dia.
